zh: 我的意思是，在 X 上，在 Instagram 上，在 YouTube 上，你看到很多人要么已经建立了全新的 AI 原生工作室，要么就是个人，你知道，运营一个品牌并扩展他们自己的内容，创作叙事故事。

zh: 像 Psyop Anime 或 Gossip Goblin 或 Charlie Curran 这样的人正在发布...

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you watch the content, it's immediately clear that one person or small teams could have never created this before AI.
zh: 当你看这些内容时，很明显，一个人或小团队在 AI 之前是永远无法创作出这些的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whether it's animation or anime or whether it's, you know, photorealistic live action, I'm not sure what you call it when it's AI, like would have required massive budgets and months to do.
zh: 无论是动画还是动漫，或者是照片级真实的真人动作，我不确定当它是 AI 时该怎么称呼，像这样的事情以前需要庞大的预算和数月的时间。

zh: 这实际上很有趣。

en: Have you had a go at creating your own?

zh: 你觉得体验如何？

en: I try to create all sorts of AI content, largely to test the tools.
zh: 我尝试创建各种类型的 AI 内容，主要是为了测试工具。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我尽量不自欺欺人地认为我有什么人们会想看的惊人故事要讲。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 但我确实喜欢在不同风格下测试各种东西，你知道，动漫、3D 动画、照片级真实，只是为了了解模型质量是如何提高的，以及驾驭方式是如何改进的。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are things about it, like we were chatting how, you know, the models have gotten so much better, but they're not perfect.
zh: 关于这有一些事情，就像我们聊到的，你知道，模型已经变得好多了，但它们并不完美。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you can spend a lot of money generating over and over and over again to try to fix a small mistake or to try to get a scene perfect.
zh: 所以你可能花很多钱一遍又一遍地生成，试图修复一个小错误或试图让一个场景完美。

speaker: Unknown
en: But at the same time, we've come super far with things like character consistency, with the physics of the real world working in most scenes, even if it's not perfect, with video models being able to follow prompts around.
zh: 但与此同时，我们在角色一致性、现实世界的物理在大多数场景中起作用（即使不完美）、视频模型能够遵循提示词方面已经走了很远...

speaker: Unknown
en: camera control and transitions and things like that much better than they used to.
zh: 在镜头控制和过渡以及类似的事情上比以前好多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's much more fun than frustrating.
zh: 所以这比令人沮丧更有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember, it must be like three years ago now or whatever, I was trying to create a super basic, it was almost like a slideshow animation of like Calvin and Hobbes, you know, through the years.
zh: 我记得，那一定是像三年前或别的什么时候，我试图创建一个超级基础的，它几乎像是 Calvin and Hobbes 的幻灯片动画，你知道，通过那些年。

speaker: Unknown
en: And oh my gosh, it took days and the output was terrible.
zh: 天哪，花了几天时间，输出结果很糟糕。

en: At the time, I was like, this is incredible.
zh: 当时，我想，这太不可思议了。

zh: 我是用 AI 做了这个。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 但那是一个非常令人沮丧的过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now I would say it's a lot more fun.
zh: 现在我会说它有趣多了。

en: Exactly.
zh: 没错。

en: I think we're still at the early infancy stages, right?
zh: 我认为我们仍处于非常早期的阶段，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I was saying before we came on, I started creating our own micro drama around the Nike story.
zh: 我来之前就在说，我开始围绕耐克的故事创作我们自己的微型剧集。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the idea was, anyone who's listening can take this idea, right?
zh: 所以这个想法是，任何听的人都可以采纳这个想法，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: all of these incredible companies we talk about on a daily basis, they all have an origin story.
zh: 我们每天谈论的所有这些令人难以置信的公司，它们都有一个起源故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But nobody actually knows a lot of the time what the origin story is.
zh: 但很多时候，实际上没人知道那个起源故事是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: How cool would it be to have an AI microdrama series called The Origins or The Tech Origins or something around how all of these incredible companies got created.
zh: 如果有一部名为“起源”或“科技起源”之类的 AI 微剧系列，讲述所有这些令人难以置信的公司是如何创建的，那该多酷啊。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anyway, I started playing around with a couple of these AI models and tools around how did my key stories, you know, journey started, The Origin Story.
zh: 无论如何，我开始尝试使用这些 AI 模型和工具，看看耐克的故事，你知道，旅程是如何开始的，“起源故事”。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the storytelling, I think, is pretty good.
zh: 而且我认为讲故事这方面做得相当好。

speaker: Unknown
en: The design, the aesthetics of the actual show is so good.
zh: 设计，实际节目的美学效果非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But maybe where it's still lagging is the camera lens, the lighting, how quickly people are walking.
zh: 但也许仍然滞后的是镜头、光线、人们走路的速度。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every AI microdrama needs some romantic story to it.
zh: 每部 AI 微剧都需要一些浪漫的故事情节。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe the romantic story for like the Nike story could be around when the founder meets Michael Jordan for the first time.
zh: 所以也许像耐克故事这样的浪漫故事可以围绕创始人第一次遇见迈克尔·乔丹展开。

speaker: Unknown
en: Michael Jordan falls in love with like this incredible shoe.
zh: 迈克尔·乔丹爱上了这双令人难以置信的鞋。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you can make it so good.
zh: 但你可以把它做得非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And honestly, I only spent like two or three hours playing around with it.
zh: 老实说，我只花了大约两三个小时来摆弄它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it was quite good.
zh: 我觉得它相当不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's in three hours.
zh: 而且那是三个小时内做出来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That sounds incredible.
zh: 听起来不可思议。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think also it's fun to think about different iterations of microdramas like that.
zh: 我认为思考此类微剧的不同迭代也很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like I think historically when people think microdramas, they think like soap operas or just kind of, you know, crazy, suspenseful, pure romance.
zh: 就像我认为历史上当人们想到微剧时，他们会想到肥皂剧或者只是某种，你知道，疯狂的、悬疑的、纯浪漫的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there's an opportunity to tell so many different types of stories like what you're mentioning.
zh: 但有机会讲述如此多种类的故事，就像你提到的那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's an opportunity for it to be somewhat educational.
zh: 它有机会变得具有某种教育意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like there's so many different sorts of content that are unlocked here.
zh: 这里解锁了如此多种类的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's pretty interesting to see the consumer adoption of this.
zh: 看到消费者对此的采用情况非常有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was actually just in China last week and seeing the adoption of technology and consumer social apps is so interesting to see versus what happens in the West, right?
zh: 我上周实际上就在中国，看到技术和消费者社交应用的采用情况，与西方发生的情况相比，真的非常有意思，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you see the adoption of these AI microdramas actually sticking around?
zh: 你如何看待这些 AI 微剧的采用能够持续下去？

speaker: Unknown
en: And is it just, are we just going for a phase?
zh: 我们是不是只是追赶一个阶段？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it just going to die or is it going to last?
zh: 它会消亡还是会持续下去？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think from a consumer perspective, my instinct at least is that people don't actually care what it's made with.
zh: 我认为从消费者的角度来看，至少我的直觉是人们实际上并不在乎它是用什么做的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, at first, maybe the folks on X or Reddit or wherever, people who care about technology and want to follow the progress may watch something because it's AI and may follow along because it's AI.
zh: 你知道，起初，也许 X 或 Reddit 或其他地方的人，那些关心技术并想要跟进进展的人可能会因为它是 AI 而观看某些东西，并因为它是 AI 而继续关注。

speaker: Unknown
en: The mass market consumer does not care that it was made with AI and isn't going to watch it for that reason.
zh: 大众市场消费者并不在乎它是用 AI 制作的，也不会因为这个原因而去观看它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the question is, do we hit the quality bar where it makes sense for all micro dramas or many micro dramas to be created with AI because it's...
zh: 所以问题是，我们是否达到了质量门槛，使得所有微剧或许多微剧用 AI 制作是合理的，因为它……

speaker: Unknown
en: you know, 90, 95% of the quality of filming, but it's so much cheaper and faster and easier.
zh: 你知道，达到了拍摄质量的 90%、95%，但它便宜、快速和容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we are quickly approaching that point where some micro dramas can be entirely made with AI.
zh: 我认为我们正在快速接近那个点，即一些微剧完全可以由 AI 制作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some are made with a combination of, you know, human filming and then some sort of AI editing, adding backgrounds, adjusting things, dubbing, that sort of thing.
zh: 一些是真人拍摄和某种 AI 编辑的组合，添加背景，调整事物，配音，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, I don't think this is a trend just because it so massively shifts the...
zh: 所以是的，我不认为这只是一个趋势，因为它极大地改变了……

speaker: Unknown
en: what the supply curve can look like because now for $100,000, you can make so many more episodes than you could make before.
zh: 供应曲线的样子，因为现在用 10 万美元，你可以制作比以前多得多的剧集。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just makes a ton of sense for the producers of the micro dramas to be using AI because historically, like one of their biggest problems was just having enough content, having the volume, having the diversity of content to be able to get viewers in and retain them on the platform.
zh: 对于微剧的制作者来说，使用 AI 非常有意义，因为历史上，他们最大的问题之一就是内容不足，缺乏体量和内容的多样性，无法吸引观众并留住他们在平台上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's also going to be interesting to see the type of content, it doesn't have to be micro dramas in this case, that individual creators create versus the micro studios, right?
zh: 我认为看到个人创作者创作的与微型工作室创作的内容类型（在这种情况下不一定是微剧）也很有趣，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we're saying, it is still pretty expensive as an individual creator to create an AI micro drama.
zh: 就像我们说的，作为个人创作者，制作 AI 微剧仍然相当昂贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like we didn't spend too much creating our own, maybe under $500, but that's still a lot and there's still these multiple iterations, right?
zh: 就像我们制作自己的微剧并没有花太多钱，也许不到 500 美元，但这仍然很多，而且仍然有这些多次迭代，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think the cost for individual creators will go down over time where you can maybe knock something out for a couple hundred dollars?
zh: 你认为个人创作者的成本会随着时间的推移而下降吗，让你也许花几百美元就能搞定一个东西？

speaker: Unknown
en: For sure.
zh: 肯定的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the trend we see with all of these models is that over time the...
zh: 我认为我们在所有这些模型中看到的趋势是，随着时间的推移……

speaker: Unknown
en: The quality that you can get for a certain price goes up, which is great as more and more new models come out.
zh: 你能以特定价格获得的质量会提高，随着越来越多的新模型推出，这很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the frontier models, like right now that's Seedance 2, will always be very expensive.
zh: 我认为前沿模型，比如现在是 Seedance 2，将总是非常昂贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's an incentive with more and more competition in the space for the model providers to both continue improving their models and also to make their models less expensive over time so more people can use them.
zh: 我认为随着这个领域的竞争越来越多，模型提供商有一种动力，既继续改进他们的模型，同时也让他们的模型随着时间的推移变得更便宜，以便更多人可以使用它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Google did this with VO3 when they released VO3 Fast.
zh: 我认为谷歌在发布 VO3 Fast 时通过 VO3 做到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we saw yesterday, SeaDance is now doing this with SeaDance 2 Fast, which is much cheaper and faster.
zh: 而我们看到昨天，SeaDance 现在正在通过 SeaDance 2 Fast 做这件事，这更便宜且更快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so my instinct is we're just going to keep seeing that the costs go down over time.
zh: 所以我的直觉是，我们将只是继续看到成本随时间下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, of course, hopefully we'll have better and better kind of frontier models that will likely stay pricey for a little while.
zh: 然后，当然，希望我们会有越来越好的一类前沿模型，它们可能会在一段时间内保持昂贵。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, and you know, I feel this has all changed in maybe six months.
zh: 是的，你知道，我觉得这一切都在可能六个月内发生了变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if you asked a regular consumer six months ago, would you watch an AI-generated movie program, whatever you call that episode, they would probably say no.
zh: 我认为如果你在六个月前问一个普通消费者，你会看一个 AI 生成的电影节目，不管你怎么称呼那一集，他们可能会说不。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I think they don't mind, right?
zh: 现在，我认为他们不介意，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: If it's good quality.
zh: 如果质量好的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, some of the most viral clips I've seen from the World Cup are like AI-generated hilarious things of like an entire team forming a circle and moving down the field to score a goal or like the Brazil team building a brick wall in front of their goal so no one can score.
zh: 我的意思是，我看过的一些关于世界杯的最疯传的片段，比如 AI 生成的滑稽东西，就像整支球队围成一个圈并沿着球场移动去进球，或者像巴西队在他们的球门前砌一堵砖墙，这样没人能得分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, it sort of just unlocks...
zh: 就像，它某种程度只是解锁了……

speaker: Unknown
en: all of this stuff, like these crazy, weird, interesting ideas that people have in their imagination that they could never make before, that they can then share with the world and a bunch of other people can be like, whoa, this is super cool or interesting or weird or entertaining, kind of whatever it's intended to be.
zh: 所有这些东西，就像这些人们想象中疯狂的、怪异的、有趣的想法，那是他们以前从未制造过的，然后他们可以与世界分享，而其他很多人可以会说，哇，这超级酷或有趣或怪异或娱乐，不管它意在成为什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: exactly.
zh: 确切地。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we're both in this new media ecosystem, right?
zh: 你知道，我们都在这个新媒体生态系统中，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, spreading so much around what's happening in the category and ecosystem.
zh: 你知道，在这个类别和生态系统中发生的事情周围传播得如此之多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one trend I keep hearing, I'd love to get your take is around, will this AI stop?
zh: 而且我听到的一个趋势，我想听听你的看法，是关于，AI 会停止吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And to turn this around, should creators be thinking about...
zh: 而且反过来，创作者应该考虑……

speaker: Unknown
en: is their content timely or timeless?
zh: 他们的内容是及时的还是永恒的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I know your colleague, Eric, did a great tweet about this recently where really the terms came from.
zh: 我知道你的同事 Eric 最近发了一条很棒的推文，术语真的就是从那里来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that how creators should be thinking about creating content to avoid potentially being accused of, oh, this is just all AI generators?
zh: 这是创作者应该考虑创建内容以避免可能被指责的方式吗，哦，这只是所有的 AI 生成器？

speaker: Unknown
en: The slop concept is very interesting to me because I think it came out around AI, but my take at least has been there's a ton of human produced slop.
zh: slop 概念对我来说很有趣，因为我认为它是围绕 AI 出现的，但我的观点一直是，有大量人类生产的 slop。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like slop is more about...
zh: 就像 slop 更多是关于……

speaker: Unknown
en: The quality of the content and the narrative and, like, what it does to your brain versus whether it's made with AI or not.
zh: 内容的质量和叙事，以及它对你的大脑的作用，而不是它是否由 AI 制作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, I think you could argue that a ton of the, like, clickbait YouTube, like, insane slime challenge, whatever, shorts that people were posting far before AI are, like, human swap.
zh: 就像，我认为你可能会争辩说，很多像标题党 YouTube，像疯狂的史莱姆挑战，不管是什么，人们在 AI 出现之前发布的短视频，都是人类 slop。

speaker: Unknown
en: And AI swap is similar.
zh: 而 AI slop 是类似的。

speaker: Unknown
en: To me, it's like...
zh: 对我来说，这就像……

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know, I guess the way I understand slop is like there's no really underlying, I don't even know if compelling, because some of them do have like compelling narratives, but they just like trigger this primal part in your brain that like makes you kind of keep watching and be hooked, even though you don't, even though it's not the highest quality story or narrative typically.
zh: 我不知道，我想我理解 slop 的方式就像是没有真正深层的，我甚至不知道是否引人入胜，因为其中一些确实有引人入胜的叙事，但它们只是触发你大脑中的原始部分，让你有点继续观看并被钩住，即使你不……即使它通常不是最高质量的故事或叙事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, yeah, like we shouldn't all spend our time watching AI slop, but I think also we shouldn't pretend that slop originated with AI because there was plenty of human produced slop content before that.
zh: 我认为，是的，就像我们不应该把所有时间都花在看 AI slop 上，但我认为也不应该假装 slop 起源于 AI，因为在此之前有大量人类生产的 slop 内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think in terms of what creators should do...
